answer-para2.content: Batching requests is a critical optimization technique that significantly enhances GPU utilization during Large Language Model inference by maximizing the parallel processing capabilities of the hardware. GPUs are designed with thousands of cores that excel at performing the same operation on multiple data points simultaneously, a paradigm known as Single Instruction, Multiple Data. When requests are processed individually, the GPU spends a considerable amount of time on overhead tasks such as memory management and kernel launches, leaving the computational cores largely idle. By grouping multiple requests into a single batch, you amortize this fixed overhead across many inputs, allowing the hardware to maintain a high level of throughput. This approach ensures that the massive parallelism of the GPU is fully exploited, reducing latency per token and increasing the overall efficiency of the inference pipeline, which is essential for handling high-concurrency workloads in production environments effectively.
